prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Health and social care
- Increase NHS revenue spending by £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Targets: shorter waiting lists; rapid GP access (same day for urgent need); universal NHS dentistry access; pay uplifts; restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn).
- Primary care: +£1.5bn annually by 2030; £2bn capital; more community diagnostics.
- NHS dentistry: investment reaching £3bn/year by 2030; preventative community services.
- Mental health: access to evidence-based therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school/college.
- National Cancer Plan focused on prevention, earlier diagnosis (75% at stage 1–2 by 2028).
- Support for assisted dying with safeguards; aim to end new HIV transmissions by 2030.

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; workforce pay/career framework; £20bn/year investment.
- Disabled people: immediate 5% benefit uplift; oppose voucher replacement for PIP; better transport and workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; sustained counselling; extend “staying put” to age 21.

Housing and planning
- 150,000 new social homes annually; end no-fault evictions; empower local rent controls; end Right to Buy.
- Retrofit/heat and adapt buildings: £29bn for homes; £4bn for public buildings; £9bn for low‑carbon heat; £7bn for overheating adaptation (first five years).
- New build standards: Passivhaus/equivalent; solar and low‑carbon heating; whole‑life carbon assessments; stronger public building control.

Energy and industry
- No new oil/gas licences; phased fossil fuel exit with a rising carbon tax.
- Electricity: wind ~70% by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end barriers to onshore wind.
- Expand grid, interconnectors, and storage; support green hydrogen for industry.
- Emphasis on community energy ownership; cease new nuclear and phase out existing.

Economy, tax, and public ownership
- Average £40bn/year investment in a green economic programme (power, buildings, rail, water/sewage, active travel, industry).
- Bring rail, water, and major retail energy suppliers into public ownership.
- Tax changes: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and property taxes; higher windfall taxes; carbon tax £120/t rising toward £500/t over a decade.
- Strengthen financial sector alignment with net zero; divest fossil assets by 2030.

Work and incomes
- Minimum wage £15/hour for all; day‑one employment rights; stronger union rights; maximum 10:1 pay ratio; extend gig‑worker protections.
- Welfare: +£40/week to Universal Credit/legacy benefits; scrap two‑child cap and five‑week wait; +5% disability benefits; maintain real pension value; +10% carer’s allowance.

Nature, animals, food
- Protect 30% of land and sea by 2030; increase DEFRA by £1.5bn; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; expanded Right to Roam.
- Annual £3bn grants for habitat restoration; rewet peat; expand woodland.
- Commission on Animal Protection; end factory farming practices such as cages and routine antibiotics; stronger marine protections.
- Nearly triple farm support to transition to nature‑friendly production; expand horticulture; universal free school meals and primary breakfast clubs.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (including £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/year for safe buildings; more SEND funding (+£5bn); end high‑stakes testing; abolish Ofsted.
- Early years: £1.4bn/year for Sure Start; extend funded childcare to 35 hours/week from 9 months.
- FE/skills: +£12bn; sixth form +£3bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore grants.

Transport
- Rail/bus subsidies to £10bn/year; £19bn over five years for public transport and active travel; rail in public ownership; £2.5bn/year for cycling/walking.
- Oppose new road building; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing later; EV scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new ICE sales by 2027; end ICE use by 2035; 20mph default in built-up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail alternative; no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Proportional representation; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; transparency and lobbying reforms.
- Defend Human Rights Act and ECHR access; restore legal aid; reform protest laws.
- Migration: end “hostile environment”; safe routes; faster asylum decisions; right to work while waiting; visa fees at cost; voting rights for visa‑holders.

Justice
- Presumption against custodial sentences under two years; expand diversion/restorative justice; invest £11bn over parliament in courts, legal aid, and buildings.

Foreign and defence
- Support Ukraine; pursue EU re‑entry (customs union and free movement steps); remove ISDS from trade deals.
- Increase aid to 1% of GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% of GNI; support Loss and Damage fund.
- Join UN nuclear ban treaty; cancel Trident; promote NATO reforms prioritising defence and diplomacy.
